Normalize a Count Table

Source: R/normalize.r
normalize.Rd

Applies one of the transformations that beta_div(), pca(), and envfit() offer through their norm argument, and returns the result. The values are exactly those that these functions compute internally.

Usage

normalize(counts, norm, margin = 1L, pseudocount = NULL, cpus = n_cpus())

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of count data (samples \(\times\) features). Typically contains absolute abundances (integer counts), though proportions are also accepted.

norm

The transformation:

  • 'percent': Relative abundance: each sample's counts divided by their sum (so they sum to 1).

  • 'chord': Each sample's counts divided by their Euclidean norm (so their squares sum to 1).

  • 'hellinger': The square root of each count divided by the sample's sum (the Hellinger transformation). Euclidean distances between the results are Hellinger distances.

  • 'binary': Presence/absence: 1 for each non-zero count.

  • 'clr': Centered log ratio: \(\log(x + pseudocount)\) minus the sample's mean of those logs, over every feature. Zeros get a value too, so the result is dense. See Pseudocount below.

  • 'rclr': Robust centered log ratio: \(\log(x)\) minus the mean log of the sample's non-zero counts, for non-zero counts only; zeros stay 0.

  • 'none': No transformation.

margin

The margin containing samples. 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored when counts is a special object class (e.g. phyloseq). Default: 1

pseudocount

Value added to counts to handle zeros when norm = 'clr'. Ignored for other normalization methods. See Pseudocount section.

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), will use all logical CPU cores.

Value

The normalized table, with the same orientation (samples in rows or columns, as given by margin) and dimnames as counts, and in the same form where zeros stay zero:

  • A base matrix gives a numeric matrix.

  • A Matrix dgCMatrix, dgTMatrix, or dgeMatrix gives the same class, and a slam simple_triplet_matrix gives a simple_triplet_matrix. Zeros are not stored.

  • A phyloseq, rbiom, or SummarizedExperiment object gives its normalized count matrix (not the object), in that object's orientation.

norm = 'clr' always gives a dense base matrix, since every zero becomes a (usually negative) value, which can take far more memory than a sparse input. beta_div(), pca(), and envfit() accept norm = 'clr' themselves and never make that dense copy, so prefer them where you can. normalize() warns when the result would have more than \(10^8\) values (800 MB).

Details

Samples whose counts are already proportions (summing to 1, within \(10^{-6}\)) are left as they are by norm = 'percent', as in the functions with a norm argument. Stored zeros in sparse input are dropped, and repeated entries of a dgTMatrix are summed.

Masking: BiocGenerics, which is attached along with phyloseq or SummarizedExperiment, also has a normalize(). Whichever package was attached last masks the other's, so call ecodive::normalize() to be sure of getting this one.

Pseudocount

The pseudocount parameter is only relevant when norm = 'clr'.

Zeros are undefined in the centered log-ratio (CLR) transformation. If norm = 'clr', pseudocount is NULL (the default), and zeros are detected, the function uses half the minimum non-zero value (min(x[x>0]) / 2) and issues a warning.

To suppress the warning, provide an explicit value (e.g., 1).

Why this matters: The choice of pseudocount is not neutral; it acts as a weighting factor that can significantly distort downstream results, especially for sparse datasets. See Gloor et al. (2017) and Kaul et al. (2017) for open-access discussions on the mathematical implications, or Costea et al. (2014) for the impact on community clustering.

See aitchison for references.

See also

beta_div(), pca(), envfit(), rarefy()

Examples

    # Relative abundances
    normalize(ex_counts, 'percent')[, 1:4]
#>        Streptococcus Bacteroides Corynebacterium Haemophilus
#> Saliva   0.469565217 0.005797101     0.000000000 0.521739130
#> Gums     0.895033860 0.004514673     0.000000000 0.098194131
#> Nose     0.021760633 0.001978239     0.492581602 0.001978239
#> Stool    0.001626016 0.993495935     0.001626016 0.001626016

    # Centered log ratios, with a pseudocount of 1 for the zeros
    clr <- normalize(ex_counts, 'clr', pseudocount = 1)
    rowSums(clr)  # 0 for every sample
#>        Saliva          Gums          Nose         Stool 
#> -2.220446e-16 -6.661338e-16  3.552714e-15 -1.110223e-15 

    # The same values as pca()'s own normalization
    a <- pca(ex_counts, norm = 'clr', pseudocount = 1, n_axes = 2)
    b <- pca(clr, n_axes = 2)
    all.equal(a, b)
#> [1] TRUE
